# Dash, jump and ability interactions

_Generated from `content/dash_flow`._

One row per hero and pair, read from `content/dash_flow/<hero>.json` by `DashFlow` (`scripts/arch/dash_flow.gd`, docs/decisions/0010-dash-ability-flow.md). A dash pair with no row buffers the press to the dash's end. "Source" is what the source hero does; "Ours" is what the game does now.

The jump, hold and move-out-of-an-ability rows are owner item 51 (docs/decisions/0015-combo-flow.md): every ability combines with Shift and jump unless its row is an exception, which carries a reason. A held slot with no hold row keeps through every move.

`[?]` in Source marks a row that exists but that no source or footage settles (no source, or "Not determinable"): it runs as the kit's default and is not guessed (docs/KIT_PARITY.md, item 20).

Ability into ability combines (both go) for every hero, except while a kit's own cast lock holds the body (Kael's Riposte guard and cleave, Sparkle's flight, Motley's Nightwell cast): a press made within the buffer of the lock's end goes when it ends, an earlier one is dropped with its deny cue (`--dash-flow-check`).

Buffer windows (the source publishes none [?]): a press held past a dash's or a cast lock's end, 0.15 s (`buffers.ability_hold` in tuning.json, owner item 32's default); a jump pressed before landing, 0.12 s (`buffers.jump`); Shift pressed during another movement, 0.18 s (`buffers.shift`); Kael's presses during a heavy move, 0.12 s (`buffers.juggernaut_heavy`, owner: about 0.1 s).

Every Hunter's air dash is its ground dash or a special one the source has, never the generic long dash on a charged press. "same" = the same move, clip and charge; "special" = a sourced difference.

## Cast into cast

The second ability pressed during the first one's wind-up and its recovery (the times are seconds after the first press), read from `into_cast` in `content/dash_flow/<hero>.json` and asserted by `--cast-into-cast-check`, which also asserts the first move still comes (a press that ends it reads "ends it"; none did in the measuring runs). "Source" is what the footage shows; `[?]` marks a pair it cannot settle.

## Cast at the top of a jump

One row per hero and slot, from `air_cast` in the same files: running, jumping and pressing the slot at the jump's top, keys held forward. "Ours" is what the next 0.4 s do to the horizontal and vertical speed against the same jump with no cast, measured headless by `--air-cast-check`, which fails when the game stops doing it. The source's falling physics (AirControl 0.015, briefs/supervive-data/supervive_physics.md:46) is what "steers as in any jump" copies. Verdict: match (the source settles it and ours does the same), owner (an owner call), or [?] (the source doesn't settle it; ours is kept until it does).

## Body turning during casts

_Generated from the "turn" block in `content/archetypes/<hero>.json`._

Does the body follow the cursor while the slot runs? `--yaw-lock-check` presses each slot with the cursor east, swings it 90 degrees at 0.1 s and again at 0.53 s, and reads the body over the next 0.23 s: free (it follows), locked (it holds) or slow (it turns at the capped rate). A recast row a hero lacks is its first cast's.
